chapter: Benny Meroff and Chicago's jazz scene
title: Nightly at the Sunset Cafe: Armstrong, Hines and Baby Dodds
summary: He goes to the Sunset every night in 1928, gets to know Armstrong and Hines, sits in with Louis, and follows him and other Chicago bands.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Listen - before you go into that -- can we back up for one thing I know you want to put on tape for 1928 - is when you started to go down to the Sunset---
CA n you put that in here now?
Is that when you were still with Benny Meroff------

Yes - I started with Meroff---- -- I mean going down to hear Louie and Earl Hines and all those guys - you know - and Baby Dodds and I used to --- there was one point there where I was never so--- I got to know Earl and Louie very well and I had a table at the Sunset -- nobody had that table but me after 11:00 o'clock---
And, sometimes, you'd be the only white face in there--
Well, not really - no -- that was really a black and tan place---
Oh yeah. As a matter of fact, there was really more white people than colored---
When they found out what was going on---
Oh, yes-- because the white people put a lot of money down there - youknow - and, so, I had a table down there and I'll never forget the night that Louie

had come once to hear me play in the theater and he asked me to play that night and I was never so thrilled in my life; I had to go out--- the checkroom - I had my horn in the checkroom and he let me play and I remember him laughing so when I played a couple of things that he did that I was influenced - you know - that influenced me and I played a couple of Louie's little things - he laughed like hell--- of course, as I said, I don't know whether he was laughing with me or at me --- but, I was very thrilled about it; I think I was about the only white guy he ever asked to sit in that band.
At this point, you were about 22 years old and he was about - let's see - he was about 28 years old - when this happened---
Yeah - I didn't realize that Louie was older than me - but I guess he is---
Yeah - he is six years older than you---

Six years--- but - you know - I followed Louie all around Chicago. He played down at a place called My Cellar -- I was down there every night -- but, you see, I was through at 11 o'clock at night and in those days I had some money and I could go to these places and I went - Coon-Sanders Black Hawks -- I didn't miss a place -- I went to all the places and I even used to go out to the Granada cafe and listen to Guy Lombardo and I sat in the Guy Lombardo Band once---
